mainTopic: חציצה in טבילה, when a נדה may immerse (night, eighth day, seventh day), and the time allowed between washing (חפיפה) and immersing.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a rule about knotted hairs blocking the water of the מקוה, and רבי יוחנן says only a single hair blocks. רבי יצחק then maps out חציצה: by Torah law, only something covering most of the body that the person cares about blocks. The רבנן added two more cases, but not a third, because we do not make a גזרה to protect another גזרה. Next, רב and רבי יוחנן argue whether a נדה may immerse by day, and רב ends up agreeing that she immerses only at night, so her daughter will not copy her too early. Some אמוראים still allowed daytime immersion on the eighth day where night was dangerous. רב פפא asks why women today cannot immerse on the seventh day, and the answer is that the חכמים forbade it in case a doubt comes up. The גמרא then discusses how long a woman may wait between washing her hair and immersing, and מרימר rules like רב חסדא as רב יימר explains. Finally, the גמרא asks whether she may wash and immerse on the same night, and רב אדא begins a story to challenge the lenient view; it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Three knotted hairs do not block; two are uncertain
steps.stepSummary: The ongoing statement about knotted hairs ends: three do not block the water, and the speaker does not know the law for two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three hairs tied together do not block. For two, I do not know.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ruling it began earlier about hairs tied in a knot during טבילה. Three knotted hairs are not a חציצה, and the speaker is unsure about two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A knot made of one hair can be tied tightly enough that water cannot get inside it. Three hairs together cannot be pulled that tight, so water still gets through. Two hairs are a middle case, so this speaker is unsure; רבי יוחנן addresses it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They block (they come between the body and the water)
A blockage that stops the water from touching the body, which can make a טבילה invalid
I do not know (the law is left uncertain)

phrases.english: Three do not interpose,
phrases.notes: This means three hairs tied together in a knot, which is the case the גמרא was just talking about.

phrases.english: two, I do not know.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁלֹשׁ אֵינָן חוֹצְצוֹת, שְׁתַּיִם אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement about knotted hairs that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three knotted hairs do not block. Two knotted hairs are an open question.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: only a single hair blocks
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says his tradition is that only one knotted hair blocks. So two hairs would not block either.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: We have a tradition only about one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the doubt about two hairs. His tradition says only a single knotted hair blocks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier view was unsure about two hairs. רבי יוחנן's tradition limits חציצה to one hair alone. That means two hairs, like three, do not block.

keyTerms.meaning: We have (a tradition) only about
One (a single hair)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
We have only one.
phrases.notes: He means his tradition only treats a single hair as blocking. So two hairs are fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the doubt about two hairs from Step 1 by limiting חציצה to a single hair.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one knotted hair blocks. Two or more do not.
steps.whatToRemember: One knotted hair blocks. Three do not. For two, רבי יוחנן says they do not block.

steps.title: רבי יצחק's rules: Torah law and two rabbinic decrees
steps.stepSummary: By Torah law, only a blockage that covers most of the body and that the person cares about is a חציצה. The רבנן added two decrees: most of the body even when he does not care, and a small part when he does care.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: By Torah law, if a blockage covers most of the body and the person cares about it, it blocks. If it covers most of the body and he does not care, it does not block. The רבנן decreed that most-of-the-body-not-caring blocks, because of most-of-the-body-caring. They also decreed that a-small-part-caring blocks, because of most-of-the-body-caring.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives the basic rules of חציצה. He separates what the Torah requires from what the רבנן added on top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things matter: how much of the body is covered (most or a small part) and whether the person is מקפיד (bothered by it and wants it removed). מדאורייתא, both must be true for it to block. The רבנן made each of the two 'half' cases block too, because each one looks like the real Torah case.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law (מדאורייתא)
Most of it (most of the body or hair)
A small part of it (less than half)
Cares about it, is bothered and would remove it
They (the רבנן) made a decree

steps.confusionAlert: Both decrees exist because of the same Torah case, רובו המקפיד. Neither decree is based on the other. This matters in the next steps.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic framework for all laws of חציצה in טבילה. Every later question about what blocks is measured against these four cases.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
By Torah law,
its majority, which he is particular about, interposes,

phrases.aramaic: רוּבּוֹ וְאֵינוֹ מַקְפִּיד עָלָיו — אֵינוֹ חוֹצֵץ,
phrases.english: its majority, but he is not particular about it, does not interpose,
and they decreed regarding its majority which he is not particular about
because of its majority which he is particular about,
and they decreed regarding its minority which he is particular about
because of its majority which he is particular about.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה, רוּבּוֹ הַמַּקְפִּיד עָלָיו — חוֹצֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the specific case of hairs to the general rules of חציצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מדאורייתא only רובו המקפיד blocks. מדרבנן, רובו שאינו מקפיד and מיעוטו המקפיד also block.

steps.title: Why not also decree on a small part he does not care about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן did not also make a small part that he does not care about block, because it looks like a small part that he does care about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them also decree on a small part he does not care about, because of a small part he does care about!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק's list. If the רבנן made decrees for look-alike cases, why did they stop at two and leave out the fourth case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic of 'decree because it looks similar' could keep going. מיעוטו שאינו מקפיד looks like מיעוטו המקפיד. So why is it not forbidden too?

keyTerms.meaning: So let them also decree

phrases.aramaic: וְלִגְזוֹר נָמֵי עַל מִיעוּטוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַקְפִּיד,
phrases.english: But let them also decree regarding its minority which he is not particular about,
because of its minority which he is particular about!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִגְזוֹר נָמֵי עַל מִיעוּטוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַקְפִּיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limits of the decrees listed in Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's list of only two rabbinic decrees.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same 'looks similar' reasoning should also forbid מיעוטו שאינו מקפיד, since it looks like מיעוטו המקפיד.

steps.title: No decree on top of a decree
steps.stepSummary: The answer: מיעוטו המקפיד is itself only a rabbinic decree. We do not make a new decree to protect another decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: That case is itself a decree. Should we go and make a decree to protect a decree?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The case we would be comparing to is already only a גזרה, and we do not stack a גזרה on top of a גזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both real decrees protect the Torah case of רובו המקפיד. A fourth decree would only protect מיעוטו המקפיד, which is itself rabbinic. The principle of אין גוזרין גזרה לגזרה stops the chain.

keyTerms.meaning: It itself is (only) a decree
A decree to protect another decree, which the רבנן do not make

steps.whatToRemember: There are four cases. One blocks מדאורייתא, two block מדרבנן, and מיעוטו שאינו מקפיד does not block at all, because we do not make a גזרה לגזרה.

phrases.english: It itself is a decree,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the case of a small part he cares about. That case only blocks because of the רבנן.

phrases.english: and shall we arise and decree a decree for a decree?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הִיא גּוּפַהּ גְּזֵרָה, וַאֲנַן נֵיקוּם וְנִגְזוֹר גְּזֵרָה לִגְזֵרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Principle-based limit: אין גוזרין גזרה לגזרה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any case that looks like a forbidden case should also be decreed against.
steps.terutzMaskana: A decree can only protect a Torah law. It cannot protect another rabbinic decree.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מיעוטו שאינו מקפיד does not block.

steps.title: רב: when a נדה may immerse
steps.stepSummary: רב says that a נדה immersing at her proper time may only immerse at night. A נדה immersing later may immerse by day or by night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: A נדה at her proper time immerses only at night. If it is not her proper time, she may immerse either by day or by night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new topic: what time of day a נדה may go to the מקוה. רב makes a distinction based on whether she is immersing at her proper time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'At her time' means right when her seven days end, which is the night after the seventh day. She must wait for night so that the full seventh day has passed. If she is immersing later, on the eighth day or after, the seven days are already over, so daytime is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is ritually impure because of menstruation
At her proper time (when her seven days end)
Not at her proper time (later than that)
She immerses (in a מקוה)

steps.confusionAlert: 'At her time' does not mean on the seventh day itself. It means the night after the seventh day, which is the night of the eighth.

phrases.english: Rav said:
A menstruating woman at her time
phrases.notes: 'At her time' means when her seven days finish, which is the night of the eighth day.

phrases.english: immerses only at night,
and not at her time
she immerses either by day or by night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: נִדָּה בִּזְמַנָּהּ אֵינָהּ טוֹבֶלֶת אֶלָּא בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the time of a נדה's טבילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At her proper time, a נדה immerses only at night. Later, she may immerse by day or by night.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: always at night, because of her daughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says a נדה always immerses at night, even when it is not her proper time. Otherwise her daughter might copy her and immerse in the daytime on the seventh day, which is too early.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Whether at her proper time or not, she immerses only at night, because her daughter may follow her example.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רב. He says that even a late טבילה must be done at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן agrees that a daytime טבילה on the eighth day is fine according to the basic law. He forbids it anyway, as a safeguard. A daughter who sees her mother immerse by day might later immerse by day on the seventh day, before her seven days are finished.

keyTerms.meaning: Her daughter following her example (copying her practice)

steps.whatToRemember: רב allows a late טבילה during the day. רבי יוחנן requires every טבילה of a נדה to be at night, so that her daughter does not learn the wrong practice.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice that women immerse at night, even when the טבילה has been delayed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Whether at her time or not at her time
she immerses only at night,
because of her daughter following her.
phrases.notes: The worry is that her daughter will see a daytime טבילה and later immerse by day on the seventh day, which would be too early.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: בֵּין בִּזְמַנָּהּ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַנָּהּ אֵינָהּ טוֹבֶלֶת אֶלָּא בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רב's ruling in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נדה always immerses only at night, because of סרך בתה.

steps.title: רב changes his mind: a נדה always immerses at night
steps.stepSummary: רב takes back his earlier view and agrees with רבי יוחנן that a נדה immerses only at night, even when she is late, because her daughter might copy her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even רב changed his mind. רבי חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: a נדה immerses only at night, whether or not it is her proper time, because her daughter might copy her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רב took back his earlier ruling from step 6. He now agrees with רבי יוחנן from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רב allowed a late נדה to immerse by day. Now a second report from רב says that every נדה, on time or late, immerses only at night. The reason is the same one רבי יוחנן gave: a daughter who sees her mother immerse by day might immerse by day on the seventh day, which is too early.

keyTerms.meaning: He took back his earlier view
At her proper time, meaning the night right after her seven days end
Her daughter following her example

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, both רב and רבי יוחנן agree: a נדה immerses only at night, so her daughter will not learn to immerse by day on the seventh day.

phrases.english: And even Rav retracted his view,
phrases.notes: This goes back to רב's ruling in step 6, where a late נדה could immerse by day.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Chiya bar Ashi said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: נִדָּה, בֵּין בִּזְמַנָּהּ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַנָּהּ,
phrases.english: A menstruating woman, whether at her time or not at her time,
immerses only at night,
because her daughter might follow her example.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַב הֲדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the disagreement between רב (step 6) and רבי יוחנן (step 7). רב moves to רבי יוחנן's position.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A נדה always immerses at night, whether she is on time or late, because her daughter might copy her.

steps.title: Local enactments allowing daytime immersion on the eighth day
steps.stepSummary: Four אמוראים, each in his own town, allowed women to immerse in the daytime of the eighth day because going out at night was dangerous or very hard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי ruled in נרש that women may immerse on the eighth day by day, because of lions. רב אחא בר יעקב did the same in פפוניא because of thieves. רב יהודה did the same in פומבדיתא because of the cold. רבא did the same in מחוזא because of the gatekeepers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists real towns where the sages let women immerse by day on the eighth day instead of at night. Each town had its own reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the woman herself, daytime immersion on the eighth day is never too early, since her seven days are complete. The only reason to forbid it was the סרך בתה worry from steps 7 and 8. Where night was dangerous (lions, thieves, unsafe gatekeepers) or very hard (cold), these sages set that worry aside as local exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: He made an enactment, a ruling for the community
The eighth day
Lions
Cold
Gatekeepers at the city gates, who were not trustworthy

steps.confusionAlert: These sages did not allow immersion on the seventh day by day. They pushed it later, to the daytime of the eighth day, which never risks being too early.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the night-only rule can be eased when there is real danger or hardship, as long as the immersion is never too early.

phrases.english: Rav Idi enacted in Neresh
that women immerse in the daytime of the eighth day,
because of the lions;
Rav Acha bar Yaakov did so in Pappunya,
because of thieves;
Rav Yehuda did so in Pumbedita, because of the cold;
Rava did so in Mechoza, because of the gatekeepers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְקֵין רַב אִידִי בְּנַרֶשׁ לְמִטְבָּל בְּיוֹמָא דִּתְמָנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting the rule that a נדה immerses only at night, the גמרא shows practical cases where immersion was moved to the daytime of the eighth day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where night is dangerous or very hard, women may immerse in the daytime of the eighth day.

steps.title: רב פפא asks: why not immerse by day on the seventh day?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests that since all women today are treated as possible זבות and count seven clean days, they could immerse in the daytime of the seventh clean day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא and אביי: since nowadays the רבנן treat all women as possible זבות, let them immerse in the daytime of the seventh day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא raises a new question. He asks whether the custom of today, where every woman counts seven clean days, would allow her to immerse in the daytime of the seventh day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Today every woman counts seven clean days, as if she might be a זבה. By the seventh clean day, more than seven days have passed since her bleeding began, so even as a נדה she would not be immersing too early. רב פפא is asking whether this removes the worry and allows daytime immersion on the seventh day.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, considering that (opens a line of reasoning)
Nowadays
Women who might be זבות (we are unsure)
The daytime of the seventh day

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא וּלְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava and to Abaye:
Since nowadays
the Rabbis have made all of them uncertain zavot,
let them immerse in the daytime of the seventh day?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא וּלְאַבָּיֵי מִכְּדֵי הָאִידָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from immersing on the eighth day to asking whether, under today's practice, immersion could happen even earlier, on the seventh day by day.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Since all women today count seven clean days as possible זבות, may they immerse in the daytime of the seventh day?

steps.title: The answer rests on רבי שמעון's reading of the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רב פפא by pointing to a ברייתא about the verse אחר תטהר. The first opinion reads it as 'after all seven days, with nothing breaking them up.' רבי שמעון reads it as 'after the act of counting,' meaning she could immerse on the seventh day itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because of רבי שמעון's view, as a ברייתא teaches. The verse says 'after, she shall be pure.' 'After' means after all of the days, so that no impurity breaks up the days. רבי שמעון says: 'after, she shall be pure' means after the act of counting, she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא and אביי answer רב פפא's question from step 10 by bringing a ברייתא with two readings of the words אחר תטהר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reading says the seven clean days must come in a row, all of them complete. רבי שמעון says purity comes as soon as the counting has been done, even partway into the seventh day. So by Torah law a זבה could immerse on day seven, and the next step explains why that still is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: "After, she shall be pure" (ויקרא 15:28), the verse about a זבה finishing her seven clean days
Impurity that interrupts the count. Seeing blood breaks up the seven clean days.
After the act of counting. Once the counting is done, even partway into day seven, she may become pure.
A woman who saw blood outside her normal time and must count seven clean days

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is NOT saying a woman should immerse on the seventh day. He says the Torah would allow it, but in the next line he reports that the חכמים forbade it.

phrases.english: It is because of the view of Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: This answers רב פפא's idea from before. Women may not immerse on the seventh day, and here is why.

phrases.english: as it is taught: "After, she shall be pure"
"After" means after all of them,
so that no impurity separates between them.
Rabbi Shimon says: "After, she shall be pure"
means after the action, she shall be pure.
phrases.notes: The 'action' is the counting. Once she has started day seven, the counting counts as done.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's suggestion from step 10 by pointing to a ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why can't women today immerse in the daytime of the seventh clean day?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because of רבי שמעון's ברייתא. The Torah would allow it, but the next line shows the חכמים forbade it.

steps.title: The חכמים forbade immersing on the seventh day
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון adds that the חכמים forbade immersing on the seventh day, because she could end up in a situation of doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the חכמים said: it is forbidden to do this, in case she comes to a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון finishes his statement. Even though the verse would allow immersing on day seven, the חכמים forbade it. This closes the answer to רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose she immerses on day seven and later that same day sees blood. Her whole count is ruined after the fact. Anything that happened between her and her husband after the immersion becomes a serious question. To avoid this doubt, she must wait for the night after the seventh day.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt or uncertain situation
It is forbidden to do so. A rabbinic ban on immersing on the seventh day.

steps.whatToRemember: By Torah law, according to רבי שמעון, a woman counting seven clean days could immerse on the seventh day. The חכמים forbade it, because blood seen later that day would undo her count. That is why רב פפא's suggestion is not followed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the practice of immersing only on the night after the seventh clean day, never during day seven itself.

phrases.english: But the Sages said:
It is forbidden to do so,
phrases.notes: "So" means immersing during the seventh day.

phrases.english: lest she come to a doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים: אָסוּר לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי שמעון's statement and gives the real reason women may not immerse on day seven
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Immersing on the seventh clean day is forbidden by the חכמים, in case a doubt comes up. So רב פפא's suggestion is rejected.

steps.title: Washing on Sunday and immersing on the third day
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a woman may wash her hair on Sunday and immerse on the night of the third day. He proves it from a woman who washes before Shabbat and immerses after Shabbat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says: A woman may wash on Sunday and immerse on the third day of the week. After all, a woman washes on ערב שבת and immerses on מוצאי שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב הונא allows a gap between washing (חפיפה) and immersing (טבילה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally washing should be close to the immersion. But when immersion falls on מוצאי שבת, she must wash on ערב שבת, because washing is not allowed on שבת. That gap is from Friday to Saturday night. רב הונא says the same gap is fine even without שבת, from Sunday to Monday night.

keyTerms.meaning: Washes and combs her hair and body to remove anything that could block the water before immersing
Immerses in the מקוה
Friday, the day before שבת
Saturday night, after שבת ends

phrases.english: Rav Huna says:
A woman may wash her hair on the first day of the week,
and immerse on the third day of the week,
phrases.notes: She immerses at night, so this means Monday night, which already counts as the start of the third day.

phrases.english: for indeed a woman washes on the eve of Shabbat,
and immerses at the conclusion of Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: אִשָּׁה חוֹפֶפֶת בְּאֶחָד בַּשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the time allowed between washing and immersing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may wash on Sunday and immerse on Monday night, since a woman who washes on ערב שבת and immerses on מוצאי שבת has the same gap.

steps.title: Washing on Sunday and immersing on the fourth day
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא extends his ruling. A woman may even wash on Sunday and immerse on the night of the fourth day. He proves it from a woman who washes before שבת when יום טוב falls right after שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman may wash on Sunday and immerse on the fourth day of the week. After all, a woman washes on ערב שבת and immerses after a יום טוב that falls right after שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא makes a second, wider ruling. He allows an even longer gap of three days, using the same kind of proof as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יום טוב comes right after שבת, she cannot wash on either day. So she washes on Friday and immerses on Sunday night, which is a gap of two full days. Since that is allowed, the same gap is allowed from Sunday to Tuesday night.

keyTerms.meaning: A Festival, when washing is also not done, just like on שבת
The fourth day of the week. Here it means Tuesday night, which starts the fourth day.

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's rule: a gap between washing and immersing is acceptable as long as it is no longer than gaps that happen anyway because of שבת, or שבת followed by יום טוב.

phrases.english: A woman may wash her hair on the first day of the week,
and immerse on the fourth day of the week,
for indeed a woman washes on the eve of Shabbat,
and immerses at the conclusion of a Festival
that falls right after Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשָּׁה חוֹפֶפֶת בְּאֶחָד בַּשַּׁבָּת, וְטוֹבֶלֶת בִּרְבִיעִי בַּשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב הונא's first ruling to a longer gap, with the same kind of proof
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may wash on Sunday and immerse on Tuesday night, since a woman who washes on ערב שבת and immerses after a יום טוב following שבת has the same gap.

steps.title: Wash on Sunday, immerse on the night of the fifth day
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא stretches the gap even further. A woman may wash on Sunday and immerse on the night of the fifth day. His proof is a woman who washes before שבת when two days of ראש השנה fall right after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman may wash her hair on Sunday and immerse on the fifth day of the week. After all, a woman washes on Friday and only immerses after the two days of ראש השנה that come right after שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third and longest version of רב הונא's ruling. He uses the same kind of proof as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Friday, then שבת, then two days of ראש השנה makes the same long gap as Sunday through Wednesday night. If that gap is allowed there, רב הונא says it is allowed on an ordinary week too. This finishes the series of three steps (13, 14, 15).

keyTerms.meaning: Washes and combs out her hair to prepare for immersion
Immerses in the מקוה
'For indeed', the word that brings in the proof
The night right after a holy day ends

phrases.english: A woman may wash her hair on the first day of the week,
and immerse on the fifth day of the week —
phrases.notes: Immersion happens at night, so this means the night that starts Thursday, which is Wednesday night.

phrases.english: for indeed a woman washes her hair on the eve of Shabbat,
and immerses at the end of the two festival days

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: of Rosh HaShana that falls right after Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשָּׁה חוֹפֶפֶת בְּאֶחָד בַּשַּׁבָּת, וְטוֹבֶלֶת בַּחֲמִישִׁי בַּשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב הונא's ruling from step 14 by one more day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing on Sunday and immersing on the night of the fifth day is allowed, proven from ראש השנה falling after שבת.

steps.title: רב חסדא rejects learning from forced situations
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא accepts the שבת and יום טוב cases themselves, but not the 'שכן' proof that carries them over to an ordinary week. Where washing right before immersion is possible, she must do it. Only where it is impossible may she wash early.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: we accept all those cases, but we do not accept the 'for indeed' proof. Where it is possible, it is possible. Where it is not possible, it is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא argues against all of רב הונא's proofs. Those cases cannot teach us about a normal week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת and יום טוב she cannot wash her hair, so the long gap is forced on her. On a regular weekday nothing stops her from washing right before immersing, so she must. A rule made for a forced situation cannot be carried over to a free one.

keyTerms.meaning: We accept all of those cases
We do not accept / do not say
Where it is possible

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule: wash close to immersion whenever you can, and wash early only when you have no choice.
steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא does not forbid washing before שבת. He agrees with those cases. He only refuses to use them as proof for an ordinary week.

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said:
All of them we say,
phrases.notes: He means the cases themselves, like washing before שבת and immersing after it.

phrases.english: but 'for indeed' we do not say.
phrases.notes: The word 'שֶׁכֵּן' stands for רב הונא's proofs, which all start with that word.

phrases.english: Where it is possible — it is possible,
where it is not possible — it is not possible.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: כּוּלְּהוּ אָמְרִינַן, ״שֶׁכֵּן״ לָא אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the way רב הונא proved steps 13–15.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A gap allowed because she had no choice cannot prove a gap she chooses on an ordinary week.

steps.title: רב יימר accepts the proofs except the ראש השנה one
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר accepts the 'שכן' proofs. He only rejects the Sunday-to-fifth-day ruling. After two days of ראש השנה that follow שבת, she should not rely on washing on Friday. She can wash at night and immerse that same night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר said: we even accept 'for indeed', except for a woman who washes on Sunday and immerses on the fifth day. The case of the end of two days of ראש השנה after שבת does not work as a proof, because she can wash at night and immerse at night.
steps.whatsHappening: A third view. רב יימר mostly agrees with רב הונא, but he knocks out the proof from step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יימר says the ראש השנה case is not really forced. When the holiday ends, she can wash her hair that night and then immerse that same night. So the long gap never actually happens there, and it proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for / apart from
It does not exist, meaning that case does not work as a proof
At night

phrases.english: And Rav Yeimar said:
We even say 'for indeed' too,
except for a woman who washes on the first day of the week
and immerses on the fifth day of the week,
since the case of the end of two festival days

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁלְּאַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת לֵיתַהּ,
phrases.english: of Rosh HaShana that follows Shabbat does not hold,
because it is possible for her to wash at night
and immerse that night.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יֵימַר אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ ״שֶׁכֵּן״ נָמֵי אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes a middle position between רב הונא and רב חסדא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'שכן' proofs work, except the ראש השנה one. In that case she washes and immerses on the same night.

steps.title: מרימר rules like רב חסדא, as רב יימר explains
steps.stepSummary: מרימר rules like רב חסדא: no learning ordinary weeks from forced situations. He also accepts רב יימר's point: after ראש השנה that follows שבת, she washes at night and immerses that night.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר taught: the הלכה follows רב חסדא, and also follows the way רב יימר explains it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on this argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From רב חסדא we keep the rule: wash close to immersion whenever possible. From רב יימר we keep the detail about ראש השנה: she should not wash on Friday but at night after the holiday, right before immersing.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught publicly
The הלכה follows
Explains

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: she should wash her hair right before immersing whenever she can. She washes early only when שבת or יום טוב forces her to. When ראש השנה comes right after שבת, she washes at night when the holiday ends and immerses that same night.

phrases.english: Mareimar taught:
The halacha follows Rav Ḥisda,
and as Rav Yeimar explains.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַשׁ מָרִימָר: הִלְכְתָא כְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the argument from steps 13–17 between רב הונא, רב חסדא and רב יימר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הלכה follows רב חסדא together with רב יימר's ראש השנה point. She washes close to immersion whenever possible.

steps.title: May a woman wash at night and immerse that same night?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a question: in an ordinary case, may a woman do her washing at night and immerse that same night?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages asked: what is the law? May a woman wash at night and immerse that same night?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question that has not been settled yet. It is setting up the two opinions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 17-18 allowed washing at night only in a forced situation, ראש השנה right after שבת. Now the question is about any normal night, when she could have washed during the day. The worry is whether washing at night, right before immersion, is good enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them, an open question the Sages were unsure about
Washing and combing the hair and body to remove anything blocking before immersion
Immersion in a מקוה

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
A woman, what is the law: may she wash at night
and immerse at night?
phrases.notes: He means the same night, with nothing done during the day before.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the special-case permission from steps 17-18 (washing at night after ראש השנה) and asks whether it applies on an ordinary night.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is washing at night, right before immersing that same night, allowed in a normal situation?

steps.title: One Sage forbids and one permits
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא forbids washing at night and immersing that night; רב חיננא מסורא permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא forbids it, and רב חיננא from סורא permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question in opposite ways. One says no, the other says yes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words here only give the two rulings, not the reasons. The dispute sets up the next step, where רב אדא challenges the lenient view of רב חיננא.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbids
Permits

phrases.english: מר זוטרא forbids,
and רב חיננא from סורא permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא אוֹסַר, וְרַב חִינָּנָא מִסּוּרָא שָׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two opinions in answer to the question of step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מר זוטרא: a woman may not wash at night and immerse that night. רב חיננא מסורא: she may.

steps.title: רב אדא brings up the story of the ריש גלותא's wife
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא challenges רב חיננא by recalling a story: the wife of אבא מרי ריש גלותא quarreled with her husband. רב נחמן בר יצחק went to calm her down, and she answered, 'What is there to do now?'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא said to רב חיננא from סורא: Wasn't there such a story with the wife of אבא מרי, the ריש גלותא? She quarreled with him, and רב נחמן בר יצחק went to calm her. She said to him: 'What can be done now?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא starts a challenge against רב חיננא, who permitted washing at night. He begins telling a real-life story, and the story continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'wasn't there such a story' show that רב אדא thinks this story goes against רב חיננא's ruling. Her answer, 'what is there now?', suggests she felt it was too late to do things properly that night. How the story ends, and how it proves the point, comes in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: A real event or story, often used as a precedent for the law
The Exilarch, head of the Jews in בבל
She quarreled, she was upset with her husband
To calm her down, to make peace with her

steps.confusionAlert: The story is not finished here. Don't decide yet what it proves; the next lines of the גמרא finish it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא לְרַב חִינָּנָא מִסּוּרָא:
phrases.english: רב אדא said to רב חיננא from סורא:
Wasn't there a story like this
with the wife of אבא מרי, the ריש גלותא,
who quarreled with him,

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְפַיּוֹסַהּ,
phrases.english: and רב נחמן בר יצחק went to calm her down,
and she said to him: What is there now?
phrases.notes: She means: what can I do about it now? It's already too late.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא לְרַב חִינָּנָא מִסּוּרָא: לָאו הָכִי הֲוָה עוֹבָדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the lenient opinion of רב חיננא from step 20 by bringing a story as a precedent.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חיננא מסורא's ruling that a woman may wash at night and immerse that same night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב אדא brings a real story (an עובדא) that he believes shows the practice went against רב חיננא's ruling. The full force of the challenge comes when the story is finished in the next lines.
